segments.title: I Am a Minor
segments.content:
At six-thirty in the morning.

Ying Chanxi got up on time to wash up.

After warming up a carton of milk and grabbing two slices of bread, Ying Chanxi went to the balcony.

She sent her father a "good morning" message on her phone, then turned on the radio that was loaded with a high school vocabulary list, and the audio for the words began to play.

Ying Chanxi stretched her body while listening to the audio, spelling the words out in her head.

After a simple stretch, she sat down on a chair by the balcony, eating her breakfast while continuing to listen to the vocabulary.

At seven o'clock, Ying Chanxi returned to the study, tied her hair into a ponytail, and began to preview her lessons.

Every half hour, she would get up to walk around, stretch her body, and glance at her phone.

Then she would dive back into her studies.

By the time she pulled herself out of her focused state, it was already past twelve noon.

She glanced at her phone again.

Her father hadn't replied.

Auntie Lin next door hadn't sent Li Luo to call her for lunch either.

Uncle Li and Auntie Lin were definitely opening their shop today, so it was normal that they wouldn't be cooking lunch.

She had told Li Luo yesterday that she needed to seriously preview her high school material, so he probably wouldn't come looking for her to hang out.

Maybe he had already called Zhao Rongjun out to play basketball?

So, it was going to be another monotonous day.

Ying Chanxi stretched lazily, ambled out of the study, and rummaged through the kitchen fridge, planning to cook some noodles for herself.

But when she recalled Uncle Li's masterful fried noodles, Ying Chanxi's mouth started to water.

The noodles she would make for herself suddenly seemed bland and unappealing.

So Ying Chanxi changed her clothes, grabbed her phone, put on her shoes, and went out.

First, she knocked on the door opposite hers. After confirming no one was home, she knew Li Luo had definitely gone out to play.

Ying Chanxi went downstairs and headed towards the breakfast shop across from the residential complex.

But as it turned out.

Just as she walked into the shop, about to ask Auntie Lin for an order of fried noodles, she saw a very familiar figure inside.

"Yo." Li Luo, at the front counter, caught sight of Ying Chanxi's delicate, oval face and raised a hand in greeting with a smile, "What would this customer like to have?"

Ying Chanxi stood at the entrance, looked at Li Luo, and blinked, thinking she had seen wrong. She took a step back, then stepped over the threshold again.

She fixed her gaze over there again and saw that Li Luo was still standing there.

Hmm... it wasn't a hallucination after all.

"Xixi, what brings you here?" Lin Xiuhong saw Ying Chanxi and immediately stood up from her chair with a smile, then shouted toward the kitchen, "Old Li! One order of fried noodles for Xixi!"

"You got it!" Li Guohong answered from the kitchen.

Ying Chanxi obediently sat down at the counter, politely greeted Lin Xiuhong, then turned to Li Luo with a look of confusion.

"I know what you're thinking." Li Luo leaned on the counter, propping his chin up with his hands and said with a grin, "This guy is usually such a slacker, he should be out playing ball with Zhao Rongjun. Why is he obediently helping out in the shop?"

Hearing this, Ying Chanxi's small face immediately tensed up: "I wasn't thinking that."

"This kid must've gotten a screw loose somewhere." Lin Xiuhong said from the side, "He got up in the middle of the night, insisting on coming to the shop to help."

"Mom, don't be so disingenuous." Li Luo glanced at his mom and said, "Your mouth has been stretched into a grin all morning and hasn't closed since. You have no idea how happy you are."

"I was just feeling sentimental that you still have some conscience, that you know how hard it is for your parents." Lin Xiuhong's touching moment was always interrupted by this brat, "It's just that this mouth of yours is still as foul as ever, you can't say half a sentence without annoying people."

At this point, Lin Xiuhong didn't want to talk to her son anymore and turned to Ying Chanxi, "What about you, Xixi? What did you do today?"

"I previewed some first-year high school lessons this morning," Ying Chanxi replied乖ly, "This afternoon, I plan to do some practice problems to get used to them. I have to report to the No. 1 Affiliated High School next week for their advanced summer class."

The independent enrollment batch for the No. 1 Affiliated High School consisted of a total of 160 students, arguably the cream of the crop in both academic performance and ability from Yinjiang District and the surrounding areas.

Every summer vacation, Yuhang No. 1 Affiliated High School would provide advanced high school training for these 160 students.

It was colloquially known as getting a special leg up.

The main purpose was to accelerate their learning of basic high school knowledge. After school officially started, because their learning pace was faster than that of regular students, they would have enough time to participate in various subject competitions.

So, although the No. 1 Affiliated High School enrolled around 640 new students each year, the students from the independent enrollment batch and those who were admitted later were very likely on completely different levels.

And a student of Ying Chanxi's academic prodigy level was definitely a target of special attention from the No. 1 Affiliated High School early on.

"Look at Xixi. It's vacation, but she still studies diligently every day," Lin Xiuhong said, turning her head to look at Li Luo.

Li Luo sighed. He was already immune to his mom's "other people's kids" spiel.

When he was younger, he would argue back, but now he just said to Ying Chanxi, "What my mom means is, studying like this is too tiring. You need to relax once in a while. You should learn from me on this point."

As soon as he said this, both Lin Xiuhong and Ying Chanxi looked at him with very strange expressions, probably both wondering how Li Luo had the nerve to say such a thing.

"Fried noodles are here!" Li Guohong appeared at just the right moment, placing a bowl of fragrant fried noodles in front of Ying Chanxi.

Li Luo also ladled a bowl of light seaweed soup for Ying Chanxi.

Ying Chanxi picked up her chopsticks, took a sip of the seaweed soup to wet her throat, and then began to eat in small bites.

"Mom, the shop shouldn't be busy this afternoon, right?" Li Luo asked.

"No, it's not busy. What's up?"

"Then I'll head back with her after she finishes her noodles," Li Luo said. "I'm going home to catch up on some sleep."

"Got it, go ahead."

So, after Ying Chanxi had finished her delicious meal, Li Luo went back with her to the residential complex across the street.

On the way, Li Luo glanced at the time and said to Ying Chanxi, "I'm going back to take a nap. I'll come over to your place this afternoon to play on the computer."

"Oh, okay," Ying Chanxi nodded in agreement.

"Want to play together?"

"I won't be playing," Ying Chanxi shook her head. "I have to preview my lessons. You can play."

"Actually, I was being serious just now."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback, a little confused. "What did you say?"

"I said," Li Luo glanced at her, "you should relax properly once in a while, do things you actually like."

Hearing him say this, Ying Chanxi subconsciously shook her head: "No, I like to study."

Li Luo: "..."

After returning home, Li Luo took a nap and then ambled over to Ying Chanxi's house.

Ying Chanxi let Li Luo use the study with the computer, while she took her textbooks back to her own bedroom desk to study.

Although they barely spoke for the rest of the afternoon, Ying Chanxi felt much more at ease than she had in the morning.

Every half hour, Ying Chanxi would take a break, get up to stretch her body, and would wander over to the study to see what Li Luo was doing.

But every time she got close to the study, she could hear the clattering of the keyboard from inside. When she actually went in, however, she would see an anime playing on the computer screen.

Ying Chanxi found it strange, but she didn't ask. She figured Li Luo was probably playing games but was afraid she would secretly tell Auntie Lin, so he always pretended to be watching anime.

So Ying Chanxi tacitly understood and went back to her bedroom to study.

...

June 20th.

Changning City, Wenyue Group, Qidian Chinese Website Editorial Department.

Qian Zhou, an editor in the metropolitan genre division, was reviewing manuscripts.

He had only been in the position for a month and didn't have many author connections. The manuscripts in his internal submission inbox were few and far between, so he could only fish for new authors in the pool of direct submissions to the website.

Scrolling through these new books, which were only a few thousand to tens of thousands of words long, Qian Zhou might have to go through twenty or so books before finding one that barely met the criteria for a contract.

As the lunch hour approached, just as he was about to fall asleep from scrolling through books, he suddenly came across a metropolitan entertainment novel.

He read the first three chapters.

The main character transmigrated to a parallel world where all the music, literature, and film works he was familiar with were gone.

As soon as he woke up, he found himself at the concert of a newly rising pop diva, chosen as a lucky audience member to go on stage and sing a song.

But the protagonist came with a system, and a single song, "East Wind Breaks," stunned the entire audience...

Editors skimmed books quickly. After a rough browse of the plot, Qian Zhou's eyebrows shot up, and he went back to read it carefully again.

The writing was straightforward and simple. The system's settings were revealed step-by-step along with the plot, without the bad habit of new authors who impatiently dump all the settings at once.

The opening of the plot was also quite a gimmick: starting with a bang at a pop diva's concert, paired with a cheat ability, quickly introducing the main storyline, resolving conflicts, summarizing gains, protagonist's progress, the next stage...

Hmm... the pacing was quite masterful.

Qian Zhou read a couple more chapters, then glanced at the author's pen name—Chong Ran.

He'd never heard of it.

Probably the alternate account of some veteran author?

Chong Ran, to reignite. Doesn't that mean to live a second life?

It must be some old codger trying to make a comeback with a new identity.

Maybe even a frequent "eunuch" who often drops his novels.

With this thought, Qian Zhou immediately sent a contract offer through the book's backend.

He had to sign it quickly before other editors stumbled upon it.

He was a new editor, after all. He didn't care what kind of old eunuch this was, as long as they could write something successful.

However, the subsequent development of this matter drove him a little crazy.

Starting from the 20th, when he discovered the book, for a whole week, this author named Chong Ran never responded to his contract offer!

Even the editor from the same division next to him had come across this book. Because it remained unsigned, it was still circulating in the pool and had caught the eye of another editor.

So, unbeknownst to him, several other editors had also taken turns sending contract offers to this book in the past few days.

After several days of no response, the editors casually mentioned it while chatting over lunch, only to discover that this author had genuinely been ignoring everyone!

After finishing his lunch, Qian Zhou returned to his desk. Unwilling to give up, he checked the author's backend information, found their QQ number, and actively sent a friend request.

In the afternoon, the friend request was finally accepted.

Qian Zhou immediately sent a message, explaining the situation and asking why the author was unwilling to sign.

The result...

Chong Ran: Sorry, editor. I'm a minor. I'm still trying to convince my mom, otherwise I can't sign the contract.

Qian Zhou: ???
